title: FBI Clinton Email Investigation ('Midyear Exam')
summary: Comey's statement: Clinton was 'extremely careless' with classified info on personal servers (~110 emails in 52 chains classified at the time of sending); 'no clear evidence' of intent; 'no reasonable prosecutor' would bring charges — declined. Briefly reopened Oct 28, 2016 (Weiner laptop), closed Nov 6 with conclusions unchanged. DOJ IG (June 2018) criticized Comey's public statements but found no evidence political bias affected the declination.
tldr: Comey's July 5, 2016 statement: Clinton was 'extremely careless' with classified information on personal servers, but no reasonable prosecutor would bring charges — so the FBI recommended none.
ai_summary:
AI review of FBI Director James Comey's July 5, 2016 statement, read in full:
- Scope: the investigation began as an Intelligence Community Inspector General referral; the FBI read all ~30,000 emails produced to State in December 2014 and recovered thousands more from slack space, other officials' mailboxes, and devices.
- Findings: 110 emails in 52 chains contained classified information at the time sent or received — 8 chains Top Secret, 36 Secret, 8 Confidential; 7 chains concerned Top Secret/Special Access Program matters. About 2,000 additional emails were later 'up-classified.' No evidence of intentional deletion to conceal.
- Verdict: 'Although there is evidence of potential violations... our judgment is that no reasonable prosecutor would bring such a case.' Prior prosecutions all involved intentional misconduct, vast quantities, disloyalty, or obstruction — 'We do not see those things here.'
- On hacking: no direct evidence the personal domain was successfully hacked, but 'we assess it is possible that hostile actors gained access.'
- Note: this statement predates the October 28, 2016 reopening (Weiner laptop), the November 6 re-closure, and the June 2018 DOJ IG report — those record-summary details postdate this document and were not in the text reviewed.
- Record summary verified accurate for what the document covers.
